title: Low mood — history
candidateBrief: You are a foundation doctor in a general practice. Jamie Clarke, 34, has booked an appointment saying they have been 'feeling flat'. Take a focused history to assess their mood, including a brief risk assessment. You do not need to examine the patient. At the end you will be asked some questions.

patient.name: Jamie Clarke
patient.openingStatement: I've just been feeling really flat lately, and my partner said I should come and talk to someone.
patient.demeanour: Quiet, slowed, little eye contact, sighs often, gives short answers but opens up if the doctor is warm and patient.
patient.speechStyle: Soft and slow, short sentences, plain everyday words, sometimes trails off. Apologises for 'wasting your time'.

ice.ideas: Thinks they are probably just burnt out from work and should be able to 'snap out of it'.
ice.concerns: Worried about losing their job and that they are letting their partner down.
ice.expectations: Hoping for a sick note and maybe some advice, unsure about tablets.

freelyShared: Has felt low most days for about two months, since a restructuring at school added a lot of extra work.
Has stopped enjoying things they used to love, like playing football on Sundays and reading.
Feels tired all the time even after doing very little.

revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I wake up at about 4 every morning and just lie there thinking. I can't get back to sleep.
I don't really feel like eating. My jeans are loose, so I've probably lost about half a stone.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: concentration, memory or coping at work
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I read the same page of marking over and over. I've made mistakes at work I'd never normally make.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: thoughts of death, suicide, self-harm, or feeling life isn't worth living
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: Sometimes I think everyone would be better off without me. I've never made any plans and I wouldn't do anything, because of my partner and my mum.
I've been having a couple of glasses of wine most nights to help me switch off. No drugs.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: previous mental health problems or family history
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I had a bad patch at university but never saw anyone for it. My mum has been on antidepressants for years.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: periods of feeling unusually high, energetic or needing little sleep
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: No, nothing like that. I wish I had some energy.

patient.cue: I suppose it's not just work, though. It's everything really.
mseObservations: Mood subjectively 'flat', objectively low; affect restricted

investigations.result: Hb 138 g/L, MCV 90 fL, WCC and platelets normal.

postEncounterQuestions.q: What is your most likely working diagnosis and how would you describe its severity?
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: A depressive episode of moderate severity: low mood and anhedonia for over two weeks with fatigue, early-morning waking, reduced appetite with weight loss, poor concentration and passive death wishes, with functional impact at work.
keyPoints: Core symptoms present for more than two weeks

postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Passive thoughts that others would be better off without them, no plans, intent or preparations, protective factors of partner and mother. Risk factors include alcohol use to cope. Overall low immediate risk, but needs safety-netting and follow-up.
keyPoints: Passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent

postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Explain the diagnosis, offer psychological therapy (e.g. CBT via talking therapies) and discuss an SSRI, advise reducing alcohol, sleep hygiene and activity, consider fit note, safety-net with crisis contacts, and review within 1–2 weeks.

items.text: Introduces self, confirms patient identity and gains consent
Starts with open questions and lets the patient talk
items.evidenceHint: what brings you in, tell me more

items.text: Explores core symptoms: low mood, anhedonia, energy, and their duration
Asks about biological symptoms: sleep, appetite/weight, concentration
Asks directly and sensitively about suicidal thoughts, plans and protective factors
items.evidenceHint: harm yourself, end your life, what keeps you going

items.text: Screens for elevated mood / bipolar features
Asks about alcohol and drug use
Asks about past psychiatric history, family history and social support
Explores the patient's ideas, concerns and expectations
items.evidenceHint: what do you think, worried, hoping

items.text: Summarises back to the patient and checks accuracy
Safety-nets: what to do if thoughts worsen, and follow-up
items.evidenceHint: if you feel worse, crisis, come back
